userStories.description:
## Scope update (2026-07-07, after c74cd5a3 one-shot drains landed)
The resident poller is gone: default deployments drain once at boot and per enqueue via detached one-shot `brain-dump verify worker --drain` processes; resident polling is opt-in (BRAIN_DUMP_VERIFICATION_WORKER_POLL=1). Ops/health work should target the new model:
- Health check: "queued jobs exist but no drain has run in N minutes" (stranded queue detection, e.g. spawn failures with no server reboot since).
- Doctor: report queue depth, last drain time/worker id, and whether a resident poller is running where one is not expected.
- Lease-aware run-round allocation: a direct `verify run` racing a leased drain hit UNIQUE(ticket_id, round) on 2026-07-07; direct runs should respect/queue behind an active lease.
- Recovery: command to requeue blocked jobs after a fix lands (today this is manual SQL/status surgery).

## Why
Once verification is automatic, a stalled worker becomes the new hidden human gate. Operators need a small, reliable control surface to see queue health, pause noisy execution, requeue recoverable jobs, and diagnose why tickets are not moving without editing database rows by hand.

## Scope
1. Extend brain-dump doctor/admin checks with verification worker health: worker enabled, queue depth by state, oldest queued age, stale running leases, last error, Playwright availability, app boot capability, and schema/version drift.
2. Add CLI read/control commands for verification jobs: list/status, pause/resume worker, requeue a dead/stale job, and mark an unrecoverable job dead with an audit comment.
3. Keep controls operator-only CLI/core surfaces; do not expose evidence writes or pass/fail mutation to MCP tools available to implementing agents.
4. Emit structured logs/telemetry for worker start/stop, claim, retry, stale lease recovery, dead-letter, and pause/resume without high-cardinality aggregate labels.
5. Add UI read-only visibility where useful by reusing the queue read model from the UI status ticket.
6. Add tests for doctor output, pause/resume behavior, requeue, dead-letter audit comments, and stale lease recovery.

## Acceptance criteria
- A user can diagnose why ai_verification tickets are not moving without running a per-ticket verification command.
- Pausing/resuming and requeue/dead-letter controls are audited and cannot certify tickets by themselves.
- Doctor reports stale worker/queue conditions with concrete remediation.
- Tests cover healthy, paused, stale, retrying, dead-letter, and schema-drift states.

## Diagnostic note (2026-07-07)
The confusing part is the blocked reason said `Verification uncertified: Command assertions passed.` That is bad diagnostics. I added a note to ticket 48f8387c so the ops/recovery ticket fixes this by surfacing the actual tripwire reason and adding requeue/rerun controls.

techStack: Database: SQLite with better-sqlite3, Drizzle ORM
State: TanStack Query for server state

dos: Use Drizzle ORM: `db.select().from(tickets)`
Use typed schema imports: `import { tickets } from "../lib/schema"`
Use `eq()`, `and()`, `sql` from drizzle-orm for conditions
Use transactions for multi-table operations: `db.transaction(() => {...})`
Use `.get()` for single row, `.all()` for multiple
donts: Raw SQL strings: `db.run("SELECT * FROM tickets")`
String-based table names
String concatenation for WHERE clauses
Multiple independent queries that should be atomic
Assume query returns what you expect without checking

dos: Use `useQuery` with `queryKeys` for data fetching
Use `useMutation` with `onSuccess` for state changes
Invalidate queries after mutations: `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.tickets })`
Use centralized `queryKeys` object from `src/lib/hooks.ts`
Create custom hooks in `src/lib/hooks.ts` for reusable query logic
donts: `useState` + `useEffect` for fetched data
Direct API calls without proper cache invalidation
Manual cache manipulation or refetch after every change
Hardcoded query key strings throughout components
Duplicate query setup in multiple components

dos: Use Tailwind classes for static styles: `className="p-4 bg-slate-800"`
Use CSS variables for theming: `var(--bg-primary)`, `var(--shadow-modal)`
Reserve inline styles for dynamic/computed values: `style={{ width: `${percent}%` }}`
Define shared style constants at module level for referential stability
Use `React.CSSProperties` type for inline style objects when needed
donts: Inline style objects for single-use styles
Hardcoded colors that don't adapt to themes
Mix Tailwind and inline styles inconsistently
Create new objects inside components that are reused
Untyped style objects that miss IDE autocomplete

dos: Use `createServerFn({ method: "GET" })` for reads, `"POST"` for writes
Use `.inputValidator()` for type-safe input handling
Return typed data directly: `return db.select().from(tickets).all()`
Use `ensureExists()` for required lookups: `ensureExists(project, "Project")`
Import from `@tanstack/react-start` (not `@tanstack/react-start/server`)
donts: Mix GET/POST inconsistently
Access raw input without validation
Wrap in unnecessary response objects
Return null and let caller handle missing data
Wrong import path

dos: Use Zod schemas for input validation: `{ ticketId: z.string() }`
Return structured `{ content: [{ type: "text", text: ... }] }` format
Set `isError: true` for error responses
Use `log.info()` / `log.error()` from `../lib/logging.js`
Include helpful error messages: `"Project not found. Use list_projects to see available."`
donts: Trust input without validation
Return plain strings
Return error text without the error flag
`console.log` in MCP server code
Generic "Not found" errors

dos: Test user behavior: what users see, click, and experience
Integration tests for workflows: test components together
Real database fixtures with actual schema
Tests that fail when user-facing behavior breaks
Ask: "Does this test catch bugs users would encounter?"
donts: Test implementation details, internal state, or private methods
Unit tests for every function
Excessive mocking of internals
Tests that break on refactoring internals
Chase 100% code coverage as a goal

epicDescription:
Replace human review entirely with an evidence-based AI verification gate. New flow: backlog → ready → in_progress → ai_review → ai_verification → done. A deterministic runner executes machine-executable demo steps against a fresh boot of the current code, capturing tamper-evident evidence (Playwright screenshots for UI steps, real HTTP request/response captures for API steps) attributed to "{provider} ralph" (claude ralph, pi ralph, cursor ralph, ...). Verification pass → Brain Dump itself sets the ticket to done (no human approval step). Fail → verification findings are filed and the ticket loops back to implementation with failed steps + evidence injected into the next Ralph iteration, repeating until clean. Re-verification always re-runs the full step suite so fixes cannot regress previously passing steps.

Epic auto-PR: when the last ticket in an epic reaches done, Brain Dump detects epic completion and creates/readies the PR itself (via gh) with an evidence-linked body — no human prompting.

Anti-fabrication guarantees: the implementing agent only authors step specs — it cannot mark steps passed, upload evidence, or set done (no MCP action exists for any of these; only the runner transitions ai_verification → done). The runner boots the app itself on an ephemeral port, records git HEAD SHA + dirty flag + boot log in an HMAC-SHA256-sealed provenance manifest, and refuses to certify runs whose diff touches the runner itself. Exception state instead of human gate: uncertified/tripwire runs and 3 consecutive failed repair loops leave the ticket in ai_verification flagged blocked/needs-attention — nothing self-certifies past a broken runner.

Foundation-first: tickets 1-2 centralize the status/workflow-step definitions (currently duplicated across ~30 code sites) and generate provider skill/prompt files from that single source, so this step — and every future step — is cheap to add for all providers.

Full plan document: see the "AI Verification Gate" artifact (published 2026-07-04).
